newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras frees former Haitian police chief.
newsitem.headline: Honduras frees former Haitian police chief.

text.p: Former Haitian police chief Col. Joseph Michel Francois was freed from jail on Thursday, two days after the United States lost a final bid to have him extradited on drug charges.
"He has just left the Central Penitentiary after they handed him his letter of freedom," prison official Alan Reyes told Reuters.

Francois, a leader in the 1991 coup against former Haitian President Jean-Bertrand Aristide, was a key member of the 1991-94 military government that stepped down under threat of a U.S. invasion. The United States accused the former chief of the Port-au-Prince police of drug trafficking.
The Honduran Supreme Court of Justice on Tuesday rejected a final U.S. appeal to extradite Francois to the United States, upholding lower court rulings that the U.S. case lacked evidence.
Francois had been jailed since March 7 when he was arrested by Honduran authorities at the request of the Americans.

The United States has said it won't give up trying to bring Francois to justice and has warned that the Francois case could lead to Honduras becoming a haven for drug traffickers seeking to avoid prosecution.
